Theme

Work & responsibility · Money, work & business

office noun

a room or building to work in

also offices, office building, go to the office, workplace

modern

Traupman 353: office (work place), officīna
Traupman 365: rēctōris officīna, the principal’s office

officīna, officīnae f.

noun, first declension

an office, a place of work

Classically a workshop or factory (armōrum officīna, Caes. BC 1.34; Cic. Off. 1.150, Lewis & Short); Traupman widens it to any place of work, an office included.

Other words

  • taberna, tabernae f. — a shop, a place of business

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Liv. 26.11.7: taberna argentāria (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. office (place where business is transacted)

    The Roman workplace on the street: a banker’s office was a taberna argentāria, a bookseller’s a taberna librāria (Cic. Phil. 2.21, Lewis & Short).

  • tablīnum, tablīnī n. — a study, an office at home

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Vitr. 6.4; Plin. NH 35.7 (Lewis & Short, s.v. tabulīnum); Traupman 125

    In a Roman house the room where the family records were kept; in our house the room where one works (see study).

See also study, job, position, office, business, post office, ticket office.

SourcesLewis & Short: officina · Lewis & Short: taberna · Lewis & Short: tablinum
